page.layout: One column of running text, one printed page on the scan (p. 162). Running head at top centre. No marginal notes. The right edge shows the neighbouring page and is not transcribed. Catchword at lower right.

main_text.p: fuimus reconciliati, falvabimur per vitam ipfius, id est, per ipsum in Cælis nunc viventem. Rom: 5. 9, 10. Creditis in Deum, & in me credite, ait Ipse ad Apostolos. Jo: 14. 1. Hinc dicitur sol Justitiæ[?]. Mal. 4. 2. oriens ex Alto. Luc. 1. 78. Lux vera, quæ illuminat omnem Hominem venientem in hunc Mundum. Jo. 1. 9. Rex Justitiæ. Heb. 7. 2. Justitia nostra. Jer: 23. 6. Justificati sumus, ut & sanctificati, per illius nomen. 1 Cor. 6. 11. Nullumque aliud nomen sub Cœlo datum est inter Homines, per quod oportet nos salvari; neque salus est in aliquo Alio. Act: 4. 12. Comparatur demum cum Adamo, qui fuit principalis causa introducti peccati, ut & Condemnationis atque mortis inde consequentis; unde sequitur, ipsum esse æque principalem causam justificationis ac salutis nostræ, quæ consistit in Remissione istius Peccati, Abolitione mortis, & collatione vitæ æternæ. Alioquin, Antitypus Typo non responderet; neque Remedium morbo æquipolleret. Collationem vero hanc ab Apostolo diligenter & accurate institutam habemus; tum Rom: 5. 12. 21. tum, 1 Cor: 15. 21, 22; & v. 45. 49.

Decimo; Quod credere, nostra Peccata deleta fuisse, per ea quæ Christus passus est, non sit ista Fides, qua justificamur; imo nullo modo esse possit. Ita Socinus, part: 4. de Servat: cap: 9. in ipso Titulo istius Capitis. At S. Scriptura ex adverso passim affirmat, Christum Passione sua [illegible, ~6 letters], id est, Pretium Redemptionis, solvisse pro nostris omnium Peccatis; quod si nobis vera, viva-que fide applicemus, tunc demum Peccata nostra actu deleri. Illud pertinet ad satisfactionem; Hoc, ad satisfactionis Acceptationem. Illud, ad salutis Acquisitionem spectat; Hoc, ad ejusdem Applicationem. Unde sequitur, eam esse veram & salvificam

page.notes: The Greek word after "Passione sua" is illegible at this scan resolution and is marked as such; it should not be guessed. "sol Justitiæ" (Mal. 4. 2) is doubtful, the first letter may be "f" and is marked [?]. The running head "sana" is read as printed and may be "fana" or "sana"; check against the title page. The line "Christum Passione sua" continues onto a line ending in "viva-" / "que", kept with its printed hyphen. Printed "istius" is transcribed as "istius".
